lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.15 - A Listen. Then act it out.

details:
Listen. Then act it out gives students the opportunity to read, listen to, and answer questions about the key vocabulary.
Listen models the correct pronunciation, stress and intonation of the target language.
Then act it out allows students to practise using the target language in a natural way.
Look for students pointing to the correct character as they speak when they are listening, and accurate pronunciation,stress and intonation when they are acting it out.
“My mum makes me a packed lunch every day. And if it’s a good day, she gives me biscuits! Let’s listen and see what our friends are eating in this story.”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.15 - B Look and choose

details: Look and choose checks students' understanding of the story and key structures and vocabulary.
Look for students accurately identifying where objects are in the story and comprehension of the prepositions.
“I keep my packed lunch in my bag until it’s lunchtime. Where was the food in the story we just read. Can you help me answer these questions to find out?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.69 - A Read and number

details: Read and number checks students' understanding and recall of the story and helps develop their awareness of sequencing and the importance of communicating events in order when telling a story.
Look for clear pronunciation and steady pacing when reading, and accurate numbering of the boxes.
“I might just have a biscuit now. Oh no - my lunch has gone! Can you help me order this story, while I look for it?”

details: Tongue Twisters: Listen and say practises the pronunciation of /a/ as a middle sound in words.
